slides.title: Numeric & Header Overview
slides.prompt: The <numeric> header provides algorithms like std::accumulate, std::iota, and std::inner_product. C++20 introduced the <numeric> and <ranges> updates to streamline algorithm pipelines.

slides.title: Summing Elements
slides.prompt: Fill in the function used to accumulate values over a range starting with an initial sum.

slides.title: std::iota Functionality
slides.prompt: What does std::iota(begin, end, val) do?
options: Fills a range with sequentially increasing values starting from val (val, val+1, val+2...)
Calculates the factorial sum of range elements
Initializes all range values to zero
slides.correctAnswer: Fills a range with sequentially increasing values starting from val (val, val+1, val+2...)

slides.title: Iota Generation
slides.prompt: Fill in the numeric algorithm that populates a vector with values 1, 2, 3...

slides.title: std::reduce vs std::accumulate
slides.prompt: What advantage does std::reduce (C++17) have over std::accumulate?
options: std::reduce supports out-of-order parallel execution because it does not require strict sequential order
std::reduce works on non-numeric types only
std::reduce guarantees left-to-right strict order of operations
slides.correctAnswer: std::reduce supports out-of-order parallel execution because it does not require strict sequential order

slides.title: Adjacent Difference
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm that calculates differences between adjacent elements in a range.

slides.title: std::inner_product Calculation
slides.prompt: What does std::inner_product compute for two ranges A and B?
options: The sum of element-wise products: (A[0]*B[0] + A[1]*B[1] + ...)
The cross product vector of A and B
The matrix multiplication result of A and B
slides.correctAnswer: The sum of element-wise products: (A[0]*B[0] + A[1]*B[1] + ...)

slides.title: Partial Sum
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm function that computes running cumulative sums of a sequence.

slides.title: std::midpoint (C++20)
slides.prompt: Why is std::midpoint(a, b) preferred over (a + b) / 2?
options: Prevents integer overflow during addition when computing averages
Works exclusively with floating point types
Compiles only if a and b are constants
slides.correctAnswer: Prevents integer overflow during addition when computing averages

slides.title: GCD Numeric Function
slides.prompt: Fill in the C++17 numeric function that computes the greatest common divisor of two integers.
